dedupe_keys.name: nist smart manufacturing systems sms test bed data

description: The Smart Manufacturing Systems Test Bed at the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology joins a Computer-Aided Technologies lab (design, manufacturing, inspection, data management and verification tools) with a Manufacturing Lab that mimics a contract-manufacturing shop, with CNC milling and turning machines and inspection equipment such as a coordinate measuring machine. Machine data are collected with the MTConnect standard and published through three channels: a volatile data stream from an MTConnect agent (current values, recent time series and a probe of all data items), a queryable data repository built on the NIST Material Data Curation System, and technical data packages that bundle design data with the associated manufacturing data. The aim is a tangible data source for developing and validating smart manufacturing and digital thread technologies. Access is free on the web; physical access to the test bed needs NIST approval and may be arranged on a cost-reimbursable basis. No licence is stated on the page read. The page was last updated on 24 June 2024. Caveats: it covers one small machining facility, and the volatile stream host did not answer from this session. For simulation it provides real machine-tool telemetry and design-to-inspection data for manufacturing digital twins and condition monitoring. Related catalogue records include Eclipse BaSyx and the PHM Society data repository.
